title: Form table
description: DESIGN.md §6.1. Forms are geometry and attachment topology — 'rules about shape, not content'. A form carries no statistics: mass, swing speed, impulse profile and durability are all derived from whatever materials end up in its slots, at the point of use.

offset.description: Top-down position of this part in the form's own frame: +x is the direction the wielder faces, +y is to its right. Purely geometric — the simulation never reads it, and a form that omits it stacks its parts at the origin.

links.description: Assembly graph edges, by part id. Heat, charge and reaction products travel along these.

strike_part.description: Which part meets the target, and therefore which part takes the equal and opposite half of every blow.

edge_area.description: Contact area of the striking geometry. This one number is the whole difference between a blade and a maul (§4.3).

leverage.description: Multiplies the wielder's strength into swing velocity.

max_speed.description: Velocity ceiling imposed by the geometry. Without it, delivered energy would fall monotonically with mass and no one would ever build a heavy weapon; with it, the best material for a given wielder is a discovery.
